A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DREST shutdownability study. Their text, figures, equations, references, and complete appendices support comparison, including the substantial revision of the proof.

before.justification: v1 reports original DREST-versus-default gridworld experiments, learning curves, and learned policies in Section 6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The trajectory-frequency discount, reward normalization, indistinguishable mini-episodes, and tabular REINFORCE procedure are retained. v2's indexed reward notation expresses the same DREST reward function.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the example gridworld, Lopsided rewards, and eight additional gridworlds. The additional gridworlds move from Appendix A to Appendix C. Training one agent across multiple gridworlds remains future work.

E2.justification: DREST agents are compared with the same default agents trained using tabular REINFORCE and coin-value rewards throughout. Newly cited shutdown approaches are discussed, not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: The reported training budgets, hyperparameters, evaluation frequency, and smoothing procedures match, including 131,072 mini-episodes for the main experiment. The generalized metrics presented in v2 Section 4 already appeared in v1 Appendix B; the evaluated metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: The lopsided-reward sensitivity experiment and additional-gridworld behavioral analyses are retained, including the Hidden Treasure exploration failure. The new conceptual appendices interpret existing evidence without adding empirical ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Both report ten agents per reward function and condition, individual learning curves with means, and Figure 6's empirical 10th–90th percentile bands. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All experimental plot and policy images are identical across versions. The reported findings also match, including near-0.5 shutdown-delay selection by DREST agents in the example gridworld and failure to collect C3 in Hidden Treasure. No experimental result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: New Appendix B introduces formal definitions and assumptions distinguishing indifference from preferential gaps, then argues that POST implies incomplete preferences. Appendix D substantially rewrites v1 Appendix B's neutrality proof using indexed policies and Equations (1)–(9), while retaining the same optimality claim.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims: DREST trains simple agents to be USEFUL and NEUTRAL, the observed shutdownability tax is small, and extension to advanced shutdownable agents is plausible.

C2.justification: v2 interprets existing behaviors through indifference versus preferential gaps and distinguishes separately trained agents from a proposed future agent trained across gridworlds. It also qualifies the example's optimal coin choices with a high temporal discount factor and removes the discussion of reward-instability tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 5's practical guidance on balancing the discount parameter and meta-episode size, including the suggestion of PPO-style clipping to stabilize large rewards. The reported numerical implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on partial preferences and multiobjective reinforcement learning, POMDPs, shutdown timers, and preference theory, including Nguyen, Hayes, Åström, Kaelbling, Dalrymple, Sen, and Gustafsson. It removes the PPO reference while retaining the IPP's broad research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the introductory motivation, expands metric explanations, and makes localized wording edits. It inserts preference appendices A–B, renumbers the existing appendices C–D, and moves the proof sketch into Appendix D. The main section sequence and most narrative remain.

P2.justification: v2 removes Figure 1's complete-preference panel and enlarges and repositions the retained panel. Other graphics are retained but resized or relocated, including grouping Figures 4–5 and placing Figures 6–7 before the discussion. The revised proof uses more displayed, numbered equations.

improvement.justification: The new preference appendices improve conceptual clarity, but the rewritten proof introduces an algebraic defect: a common constant term that cancels in Equation (7) remains in Equation (8), supporting a strict-increase claim even in the first-episode case where v1 allowed equality. With unchanged empirical evidence and removed stability guidance, the benefits and harms leave the net quality direction uncertain.
